title: What part of your workflow is AI?
author: VoidFullOfDreams
selftext: I am curious what is the max you can achieve in certain aspects of gamedev with AI tools. Like, if you want to make graphics, will it look good? Does it have to be styled, or can be photorealistic? Can you create all assets with AI? Write code without knowing how to? In which areas AI tools are strong, and where they don't do enough?

comments.author: Ive_Tried_My_Best
comments.body:
Four of us are making an anime-style visual novel after work. Here's where AI ended up in our workflow:

\- Story: written by us. AI only proofreads.

\- Art: AI does the first composition, and most of the time goes into manual fixing it afterwards. Hands, hair colour under different lighting, clothes that don't match what the script says, accessories moving between images. Without a reference sheet per character and a checklist for every image, things drift fast.

\- Music and sound effects: some AI-generated.

\- Code: AI writes a lot of it, but we still review and playtest everything ourselves.

\- Translation: AI does the first draft into three languages.

On your style question: stylized anime art has worked much better for us than photorealistic. Mistakes are easier to spot and much easier to fix by hand.

comments.author: algorys
comments.body:
For my part, it was mainly the graphics. It actually took me quite a while to establish a consistent visual style across the interface, buttons, creatures, player characters, world maps, and locations.

For certain elements, specifically creatures that don’t exist anywhere else, I had to create sketches first to ensure the final result was polished.

comments.author: Nostradamivre
comments.body:
The “wiring-up” part, building a library of 200, 400, 600+ items one by one, was killing all my personal time. I can code my project 100% myself, but come on, everyone knows that sprint where you have to fill everything up with content. That’s gone now.  
  
Also, I don’t use AI for any visual assets. Just use industry-standard tools, or set aside $100 for 3D models and asset bundles. That can save you 200 to 400+ hours of just lame work.

comments.author: ass-gas-hotbox
comments.body:
Experimentation to test results, and then a second pass for cleanly architecting it. 

I hire artists and musicians. I don't even mind if they use AI in part of their process. it's pretty easy to tell whether or not a body of work is a single high level prompt or if there was interaction and curation.

comments.author: VoidFullOfDreams
comments.body: I haven't tried all the areas, that is why i am asking. What i found is that VO can be excellent if you find the right models with enough emotional range. 2d art can be good enough, but haven't tried the animations. The music is awesome, but needs a lot of time to get what you want. Cutscenes... super janky unless you pay for ultra expencive models like seedance. Rest - haven't tried yet. Don't know if i should even try the code without knowing how it should function at all.
